subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode blocker is fixed, should OpenClaw accept `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`, its packaged executor binaries, transitive `node-pty` build script, and argv-carried base64 config for this official external Windows sandbox plugin?
rationale: The remaining non-mechanical choice is whether this native sandbox executor dependency graph and upstream process-argv config transport are acceptable for a first-party plugin release.

options.title: Fix Registration, Then Approve Exact Head
options.body: Add the full-registration guard and regression test, then approve the current exact dependency/security boundary if secops review accepts the MXC SDK preview contract.

options.title: Require A Safer Transport First
options.body: Pause the PR until upstream MXC or OpenClaw provides a config transport that does not place the encoded sandbox envelope in process argv.

options.title: Incubate Outside First-Party Release
options.body: Keep the work out of the official plugin release path until the dependency, packaging, and sandbox boundary are mature enough for OpenClaw to own.

recommendation.title: Fix Registration, Then Approve Exact Head
recommendation.body: Add the full-registration guard and regression test, then approve the current exact dependency/security boundary if secops review accepts the MXC SDK preview contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the live assignee and is also tied to the sibling OpenShell sandbox backend precedent used for the remaining product/security call.
